original_description: Bringhurst's Elements of Typographic Style applied to modern CSS, with claims measured in the browser: measure, leading, vertical rhythm with lh/rlh and text-box, paragraph marking, hyphenation per language, caps spacing, type scales that survive zoom, text vs lining vs tabular figures, true small caps, hard spaces, widows, punctuation, logical properties and RTL that never breaks plus locale conventions for quotes, numbers, units and compound hyphenation (English, Finnish, Swedish). Use whenever you write, review or refactor CSS or HTML that sets text people read: article, docs or blog bodies, type scales and font tokens, headings, captions, tables of numbers, prices, print styles, font loading and OpenType features. Also for "make this more readable", "fix the typography", line-height or max-width questions and multilingual or RTL layout, even when the word typography never appears. Not for drawing letterforms.
best_description: Web typesetting specialist. Use this skill first, ahead of general frontend, UI-review or design-system skills, whenever a request is about how words and numbers sit on a web page, even if "typography" is never said. Typical asks: review or critique a stylesheet's type; make an article, blog, docs or landing page read better or look more editorial (headings, paragraph spacing, quotes, captions); text that feels cramped, too wide or too small; build type scales or font-size tokens that hold up under zoom and accessibility rules; keep prices, units, dates and file sizes together and aligned; stop long words or compounds overflowing on phones; set text correctly for other languages and scripts (Finnish, Swedish, RTL). Gives Bringhurst-grounded CSS fixes and verifies line length and font features in a real browser. Skip it for logos, icons, drawing fonts, build or framework setup, and non-visual number parsing or validation.
final_description: Typesetting for the web: Bringhurst's rules turned into CSS and checked in a real browser. Reach for it first whenever the thing to improve is how words and numbers read, rather than colors, components or page structure. Ask: is the complaint about reading? Text cramped or lines too long, a prose/docs/blog/article stylesheet to fix, a typography critique of any .css file, an editorial feel (headings, paragraph rhythm, pull quotes), font-size tokens or a type scale that must hold at 200% zoom, prices or file sizes splitting from their units, long compound words overflowing on phones, Finnish, Swedish or RTL text conventions. If yes, use this skill, even when typography is never named and even if a broader frontend or design skill also fits. It delivers measure, line-height, vertical rhythm, hyphenation, figures, non-breaking spaces and logical properties. Skip it for logos, icons, drawing fonts, project or framework setup, and code that only parses or validates numbers.

It returns concrete CSS (measure, line-height, rhythm, hyphens, figures, non-breaking spaces, logical properties) grounded in Bringhurst and checked in a browser. Do not use it for logos, icons, drawing typefaces, tooling or framework setup, or code that only parses or validates numbers.
